verdicts.proposal_name: P1: Restore/overshoot the idiosyncratic cash-flow band (0.1 -> 1.75) + ivol characteristic
verdicts.critique:
I re-ran this myself rather than trusting the numbers, and three things came out badly.

(1) THE REPORTED SPAN NUMBERS USE THE WRONG WEIGHT SPACE. A linear characteristic method delivers stock weights w = X a (FM's portfolios are the columns of X pinvh(X'X), fama_functions.py:152-165, so the MVE over those factors lies in col(X)). The attainable Sharpe is sqrt(rp' X (X'Sigma X)^{-1} X' rp). Proposal 1 (and the earlier BGN diagnosis) report a projection corresponding to w = Sigma^{-1} X a instead. I verified both on the same cross-section (N=1000, band=0.1, X=[1,log mve,bm]): w=Xa gives 69.4% of max_sr; w=Sigma^{-1}Xa gives 83.4%. The 91.7%/95.03% figures throughout the diagnosis phase are the wrong object and every headroom number needs recomputing.

(2) THE PROPOSAL LEAVES EXPECTED RETURNS EXACTLY TWO-DIMENSIONAL AND EXACTLY LINEAR. From panel_functions_bgn.py:172-186: term1 and term3 are date-level scalars, term2 = pi*A*e_t/bond_t with A = P - G_t (lines 153, 161-164), term4 = Chat*pi*book. Hence 1+eret_i = [pi*e_t/bond_t] + [term1+term3-pi*G_t*e_t/bond_t]*(1/mve_i) + (Chat*pi)*bm_i, with bm coefficient identically Chat*pi = 0.0244763. sigmaj appears nowhere in that block. So after Proposal 1 the true risk premium is still an EXACT affine function of two characteristics, and the entire claimed DKKM advantage is the ability to invert a diagonal matrix. That is inverse-variance weighting, not the virtue of complexity.

(3) THE HEADLINE IS FM GETTING WORSE, NOT DKKM GETTING BETTER. My corrected ceilings at the production N=1000 (mean over t=250,260,270, seed 0): band 0.1 -> FM+ivol 0.926, RFF360 0.993, max_sr 0.3315; band 1.75 -> FM+ivol 0.721, RFF360 0.926, max_sr 0.2559. DKKM's ABSOLUTE population Sharpe falls from 0.329 to 0.237. A table showing 'DKKM/FF rises to 1.4x' while the true maximum Sharpe and every method's absolute Sharpe fall reads as a metric artifact.

DISCLOSURE: the line being changed is panel_functions_bgn.py:54, carrying the comment '# added a factor of 0.1'. Multiplying a hand-inserted fudge factor by 17.5x, in the one direction that produces the desired result, after that result failed to appear, is exactly what a referee is hunting for. Defensible only if presented as a calibration correction on its own merits with the full moment scan disclosed, including the settings that do NOT deliver the result.

Minor: the calibration table is not reproducible in detail. At m=1.75 I measure median stock vol 11.1%/mo but MEAN 14.9% (heavy-tailed), pairwise corr 0.150, sd(log d) 1.12. Close enough to the claimed 12.3%/0.220/1.212 to accept, but the mean-vs-median distinction is doing real work and is undisclosed.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: The direction replicates — I get the DKKM/FM population ceiling rising from 1.072x to 1.285x — but it collapses under the one robustness check every referee will demand. The proposal's own logic says the target is w* ~ (rp - Bc)/d, a ratio. So hand FM the ratio. I added two columns to FM's raw basis, bm/ivol^2 and log(mve)/ivol^2: at band 1.75 FM goes 0.7205 -> 0.9095 against RFF360's 0.9257. The DKKM/FM ceiling collapses from 1.285x to 1.018x. A LINEAR method with two hand-built interaction terms captures 98% of what a 360-feature random-Fourier basis captures. The 'complexity' on display is a single product of two supplied characteristics, available to FM at zero cost. FF is genuinely disadvantaged (tercile step functions cannot track a variable spanning four orders of magnitude), but FF is the weak benchmark; FM is the one that matters and FM survives. Second, because rp stays exactly in span{1, 1/mve, bm}, the gap is purely the D^{-1} tilt, which under exact K-factor pricing shrinks as N grows — my N=250 vs N=1000 comparison already shows the linear span's shortfall is N-sensitive, and a referee will ask for N=5000.
verdicts.salvage: Ship the band change as a CALIBRATION CORRECTION, argued and disclosed on its own moment-matching merits (the current model has 5.4%/month stock volatility, 0.60 average pairwise correlation, sd(log idiosyncratic variance) 0.17 — all indefensible), made BEFORE and INDEPENDENTLY of any complexity result, with the full scan m in {0.1,1.0,1.25,1.5,1.75,2.0} and all four moment targets in an appendix table. Prefer m=1.5 (median vol 7.8%, pairwise 0.27, sd(log d) 0.74) over 1.75 if you want to avoid a 63,000x d-ratio and the conditioning exposure. Then state honestly that this buys a population ceiling ratio of at most ~1.29x, that it vanishes once the linear benchmark gets ratio characteristics, and that it leaves the cross-section of expected returns exactly two-dimensional. It is a precondition for Proposals 2/5, not a result.

verdicts.proposal_name: P2: Project-scale / intangible-capital wedge kappa breaking the rp = a + b/mve + Chat*pi*bm identity
verdicts.critique:
This is the only proposal that attacks the actual binding constraint, and its central claim is correct — I verified it analytically from the code, not by simulation. panel_functions_bgn.py:172-186 gives 1+eret_i = pi*e_t/bond_t + [term1+term3-pi*G_t*e_t/bond_t]*(1/mve_i) + Chat*pi*bm_i, with the bm coefficient exactly Chat*pi = 0.0244763 at every date. Two characteristics span the entire cross-section of true expected returns EXACTLY. That identity is why nothing can beat FM here, and P2 is one of only two proposals (with P5) that breaks it. P1, P3, P4 and P6-without-BETA_ZR all leave it intact and can therefore only ever compete on the covariance side.

The mechanism is also the right KIND of economics. A latent state (economic capital Lambda) observable only through a noisy signal (payout yield) whose precision varies across firms (with project count and cash-flow volatility) makes the efficient predictor a firm-specific shrinkage weight times the signal. That is a genuine three-way interaction; it is precisely why DKKM's five-characteristic real-data result works while these models' five characteristics do not; and it is defensible as economics rather than as a basis trick. The intangible-capital framing (book value ceases to measure economic capital) is standard and publishable — Peters-Taylor, Eisfeldt-Papanikolaou. It also raises cross-sectional predictive R^2 from 0.043%/month, an order of magnitude BELOW real data, toward ~0.5%, fixing a calibration defect the paper should want fixed anyway.

WHAT IS MISSING, and it is serious: NOTHING HERE WAS SIMULATED. Every number in the predicted-effect block is derived, and the author says so. P1 at least has measurements (albeit against the wrong projector). Before this appears in a paper you need the population ceiling computed the way I computed P1's — FM basis vs RFF basis vs true max_sr, at N=1000, over multiple months and seeds.

Second, the implementation risk is real and correctly identified. kappa must appear once on col1 and col3 (sdf_compute_bgn.py:162,164), NOT inside the exponentiated col2 (line 163), twice outside the exp on term4, and squared on three diagonal corrections (lines 220-231, 234-256, 259-265) plus term2t (lines 214-218). Any one of those wrong silently biases cond_var with no exception — exactly the failure mode already documented for KP14's integ_results.npz. The proposed Monte Carlo validation (simulate R_{t+1} at fixed t, check the empirical second moment against sdf_loop's ER elementwise) is not optional; it is the referee's minimum bar and belongs in an appendix.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: Partly, and less than claimed. The honest adversarial reading: FM is not restricted to one characteristic per signal. The econometrician can construct payout*nproj, payout/ivol^2, payout*ivol and hand them to FM, exactly as I did to kill P1. The optimal shrinkage pi_i = s^2/(s^2 + noise_i^2/(num_i*H)) is a smooth monotone function of a single scalar index, so a second-order expansion in that index times the signal — three linear columns — recovers most of it. My P1 experiment is the precedent: two hand-built ratio columns closed a 1.285x gap to 1.018x. I would expect FM augmented with {payout, payout*nproj, payout/ivol^2} to recover 80-90% of the DKKM ceiling, leaving ~1.1-1.2x rather than the claimed 1.2-1.35x. The defensible position is not 'FM cannot do this' — it can, given the right constructed columns — but 'FM cannot do this without the econometrician already knowing the structural shrinkage formula.' That is a genuine and honest statement about what complexity buys; say it, and pre-commit to a characteristic set chosen without reference to the structural solution. Note also that the two channels can cancel: at P1's band the payout signal may be so noisy that optimal shrinkage is near zero and the channel dies — the author flags this, and it must be checked before implementation, not after.
verdicts.salvage: Keep as the centrepiece with four required changes. (a) Simulate it and report the population ceiling with the CORRECT w = Xa projector at N=1000 across months and seeds, before writing prose. (b) Frame it as unmeasured intangible capital, cite the accounting literature, and calibrate SIGMA_KAPPA to an independently measured moment (sd of the economic-to-book capital ratio, or the cross-sectional R^2 of returns on chars) — never to the DKKM/FM gap. (c) Give FM and FF the payout characteristics AND at least one constructed interaction, and report the gap that survives; a gap existing only because the linear benchmark was denied an obvious column is not a result. (d) Ship the elementwise Monte Carlo validation of ER as an appendix table. Done this way it is publishable economics: it fixes the model's cross-sectional R^2, it is motivated by a large empirical literature, and its nonlinearity is a consequence of signal extraction rather than an assumption.

verdicts.proposal_name: P3: Repair agr, add characteristics, rescale GAMMA_GRID, NMAT=1, recentre ALPHA_LST
verdicts.critique:
This is two proposals wearing one coat, and they deserve opposite verdicts.

THE BUG FIXES ARE MANDATORY AND MUST NOT BE BUNDLED. agr is 91% ties at exactly zero because book = I*num (panel_functions_bgn.py:144) is a small integer, and dkkm_functions.rank_standardize breaks the ties with np.argsort (line 57), manufacturing a persistent pseudo-random column that enters all 3600 RFF features multiplicatively but only one of FM's six regressors additively. The FF cma sort is simultaneously degenerate (q30 = q70 = 0, so the '2x3' is a 92/0/8 split with literally empty middle portfolios). These are defects, they are asymmetric, and they must be repaired regardless of what happens to the model. Repair them in a separate commit, re-run the baseline, and report the corrected baseline BEFORE any model change. If the corrected baseline moves at all, the currently published tables are wrong and that belongs in the paper.

THE DKKM-ONLY KNOBS ARE THE PROBLEM. GAMMA_GRID rescaling, NMAT 5->1, and recentring ALPHA_LST are three tuning changes applied to exactly one of three competing estimators, after that estimator was observed to lose. Meanwhile config.py:187 sets ALPHA_LST_FAMA = [0] — FF and FM get no regularization and no tuning at all — and bop-analyze-remote/create_slides_tables.py:83-97 (find_best_alpha_for_model) selects DKKM's alpha by argmax of the evaluation metric itself across all iterations. As the pipeline stands, DKKM already gets post-hoc selection over 6 alphas x 4 feature counts using the reported statistic, and FF/FM get zero tuning decisions. Adding three more DKKM-only knobs is indefensible and cannot be buried: the alpha grid is in config.py and a referee will read it.

AND THE BANDWIDTH KNOB DOES NOT WORK. I tested it directly on BGN's true moments, N=1000, RFF with 360 features: gamma x1 gives ceiling 0.9931 (band 0.1) and 0.9257 (band 1.75); gamma x3.44 gives 0.9931 and 0.9303; gamma x8 gives 0.9763 and 0.8927. The recommended rescale is worth +0.5 percentage points at band 1.75 and exactly zero at baseline; the larger rescale is actively harmful. The a priori argument (match DKKM's L=130 effective sd(Wx)) is principled and pre-registerable, which is its saving grace — but it belongs in a robustness column, not the main specification.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: No, and the proposal concedes ~1.05x standalone. My measurements agree: the bandwidth rescale is worth +0.005 of ceiling. Worse, the characteristic-addition half actively HELPS the competitor. At the current calibration FM with the raw five characteristics reaches 0.810 of max_sr, but FM with ivol added reaches 0.926 — adding one characteristic closed most of FM's shortfall and cut the DKKM/FM ceiling from 1.23x to 1.07x. So 'give the econometrician more characteristics' is, in this model, a PRO-FM intervention. It becomes pro-DKKM only if the added characteristics enter the truth nonlinearly, which requires a model change first. The proposal is honest about this ('only ship with a model change whose target is demonstrably nonlinear'), and that honesty is correct.
verdicts.salvage: Split into three commits with three justifications. (1) BUG FIXES, unconditional: 12-month agr, and either drop the degenerate cma factor or document the empty middle portfolios. Re-run and republish the baseline. (2) CHARACTERISTIC SET, chosen and frozen BEFORE seeing any complexity result, justified by 'what would a real econometrician observe from this firm', and identical for FF, FM and DKKM. Include 1/mve as well as log(mve) — see my missed-ideas list; rp is exactly affine in 1/mve, so denying FM that transform is a live, undisclosed handicap. (3) ESTIMATOR HYPERPARAMETERS: whatever you do to DKKM's regularization you must do to FF/FM. Give FF/FM the same ridge grid, and either drop the post-hoc argmax in find_best_alpha_for_model in favour of a fixed pre-specified alpha, or apply identical post-hoc selection to FF/FM and disclose it in the table caption. The bandwidth rescale goes in a robustness appendix with the measurement that it is worth +0.5pp.

verdicts.proposal_name: P4: Cohort (vintage) common cash-flow factors with age-dependent exposures
verdicts.critique:
The construction is elegant and the code path is right: cohort shocks are orthogonal to nu, so cov(log M, log C_j) = -beta_j is preserved, risk-neutral project value stays Chat*exp(-beta_j), and Jstar.csv/optval need no re-solve. I checked lines 69-76 and 148-186 and agree that prices, the exercise rule and the entire eret vector are untouched.

But that last point is the problem, not the feature. Because eret is untouched, the true conditional risk premium remains EXACTLY affine in (1/mve, bm) with bm coefficient Chat*pi = 0.0244763. Proposal 4 is, like Proposal 1, a pure covariance-side intervention. The paper's claim would be 'complexity pays because it hedges unpriced factors better' — a statement about covariance estimation, not the DKKM/AIPT mechanism (unspanned expected-return components spread across many eigenvalue directions). A referee who knows that theory will say you have demonstrated a different phenomenon and mislabelled it.

The dimension-counting argument is weaker than presented. 'With L=6 chars and K_eff=20 cohort factors, FM attains at most sqrt(6/20)' holds for a generic exposure vector Theta; the actual Theta is highly structured (project age distributions are smooth, geometric-tailed, and near-identical across firms because pi = 0.99 is common to all), so exposures will be dominated by two or three principal components that a linear method hedges easily. The proposal concedes this and proposes the right pilot diagnostic; until it is run this is speculation.

Finally: the magnitude is admitted to be the least certain of the six, it REQUIRES Proposal 1 to have room to operate, and it adds a second sparse kron to the O(N^2) inner loop in a moments step already pinned to n_jobs = 1 (config.py:40).
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: Probably not, and there is a clean referee counter. Firm i's exposure to cohort m is phi_m(i) = the value share of its live projects born in window m — which is LINEAR in observable age-composition shares. In real data researchers routinely control for industry and vintage with dummy variables, a purely linear device. So the natural benchmark is not FM-on-six-scalars but FM augmented with age-bucket portfolios, which spans the cohort exposure space exactly and hedges perfectly by construction. The entire proposed advantage rests on the econometrician being handed a scalar 'age' rather than age-bucket weights — an information restriction the authors chose. A referee will ask 'why can't the econometrician sort on age deciles?' and there is no good answer. Separately, cohort factors carry no premium, so max_sr falls: like P1, this improves the RATIO by degrading the benchmark rather than giving DKKM anything new to find.
verdicts.salvage: Only worth doing if the pilot diagnostic passes: at a single month, compute the FM-span-optimal portfolio's implied cohort exposure vector and show it is materially nonzero AND not spanned by age-decile portfolios. If it passes, the defensible version is not 'cohort' but a genuinely PRICED second aggregate factor — an investment-specific technology shock with a nonzero price of risk and characteristic-dependent loadings — which would break the affine identity and raise the effective rank of the priced-risk space, the condition the theory actually requires. As specified (unpriced, hedge-only) I would not run it: highest implementation risk of the covariance-side proposals, smallest defensible payoff, most obvious referee counter.

verdicts.proposal_name: P5: Characteristic-dependent clientele demand wedge (an AIPT alpha)
verdicts.critique:
The economics is right and the implementation is fatal, and the proposal says the fatal part out loud: 'choose h to be exactly orthogonal, in each monthly cross-section, to {1, size, bm, agr, roe, mom} and to the six FF factor weight vectors, by projecting the candidate h onto those columns and subtracting. Then the FM-attainable Sharpe from the alpha channel is exactly zero.'

That is not a model. That is constructing a signal in the null space of the competitor and then reporting that the competitor cannot find it. The author calls it 'a theorem rather than an approximation argument' — it is a theorem, and that is precisely the objection. THIS IS THE SENTENCE THAT KILLS THE PAPER: 'The authors orthogonalise the mispricing against the benchmark's span by construction and then report that the benchmark cannot price it.' No revision recovers from it.

Compounding it: the orthogonalisation is against the LINEAR char span while h is left inside the nonlinear span of the same characteristics. The wedge is engineered to be invisible to FM and visible to DKKM using the very basis distinction the paper purports to test. Not a subtle specification-search problem — the answer is written into the data generating process.

Three further problems each requiring major revision. (i) It changes what 'true' means: rp, cond_var, max_sr and sdf_ret become the marginal investor's objects rather than the representative agent's, so the HJ bound and every HJD number change meaning and must be re-derived. (ii) At the calibrated S* ~ 1.1/month the HJD metric degenerates (E[sdf_ret] -> Rf, sd(sdf_ret) -> 0), so half the paper's evidence base becomes uninformative exactly when the result appears. (iii) The wedge target must use only date-t information for ER to stay analytic, ruling out the natural specification (a wedge on the contemporaneous valuation ratio) and forcing an arbitrary one-month lag.

To be fair on one point: the underlying diagnosis is correct and important. No frictionless representative-agent model with a rank-1 price-of-risk vector can produce a 3-5x complexity advantage; my own numbers agree (the best any covariance-side change achieves is a 1.29x ceiling that collapses to 1.02x under an obvious check). If the paper wants a real-data-sized result, something like this is the only route. The idea is right; the execution assumes the conclusion.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: Yes — trivially, tautologically, and that is exactly why it is worthless as evidence. Define h orthogonal to the FF/FM span and inside the RFF span, and FM's attainable alpha Sharpe is zero by construction while DKKM's is whatever THETA_W is set to. The gap is a free parameter. The interesting counterfactual is the one not run: an ECONOMICALLY specified h with no orthogonalisation. A plausible demand wedge (a small-value-high-volatility tilt, say) loads heavily on the linear characteristic span, because that is what the anomaly literature's characteristics ARE. My P1 experiment is the relevant evidence: even a genuinely nonlinear target (the 1/d ratio tilt) was 98% recovered by a linear method given two constructed columns. I would expect a non-orthogonalised demand wedge to deliver 1.2-1.6x, not 2.5-4x. That number would be a real finding; the orthogonalised number is not.
verdicts.salvage: Replace the orthogonalisation with a specified demand system. Write the wedge as arising from a Koijen-Yogo style clientele whose portfolio weights are a parametric function of characteristics with parameters taken from the estimated demand-system literature — not chosen, and explicitly NOT orthogonalised against anything. Report the resulting DKKM/FM gap, whatever it is, and report separately how much of the wedge lies inside the linear char span (a number the paper should want to disclose: it is the fraction of real-world 'alpha' a linear factor model can reach). Keep the calibration discipline already present (anomaly half-life 1-3 years -> RHO_U = 0.97; anomaly spread -> sd(alpha) ~ 36bp/month) and state up front that the paper is now about a segmented-clientele economy, with rp and the HJ bound reinterpreted accordingly. Switch HJD to the scale-free sqrt(1 - rho_uncentered^2) BEFORE running this or the metric will hide the result. Done that way it is a legitimate and interesting paper; done as written it is unpublishable.

verdicts.proposal_name: P6: Heterogeneous project durability (discrete survival types), optionally with larger |BETA_ZR|
verdicts.critique:
Worst payoff-to-risk ratio of the six, and the author essentially concedes it ('I rank it last on impact per unit of work').

Credit where due: durability types DO perturb the affine identity, since A = book*Chat*beta_avg*bond_values (line 153) no longer uses a single bond value — it is the only covariance-side proposal that touches the premium at all. But the perturbation is tiny, because the interest-rate factor is nearly unpriced: lambda_xi/lambda_mu = -0.178, from BETA_ZR = -0.00014 and SIGMA_R = 0.002 (config.py:200-204). Duration heterogeneity moves expected returns almost not at all unless BETA_ZR is also raised.

And raising BETA_ZR is not a free rider. BETA_ZR enters vasicek.py's sigma12 recursion (lines 35-42) and therefore B(k,r), D(r), prob_in_money, and the beta_star/scale calibration (lines 68-77). Change it and you must re-fit the beta distribution and regenerate Jstar.csv, and every calibrated moment (E[num], mean bm, mean mve) moves. That is a full recalibration presented as a parameter tweak.

The decisive objection is operational. This is the only proposal requiring a shipped solution file to be regenerated, once per durability type, via the commented-out triple-nested-sum code at vasicek.py:123-174, with no correctness test beyond an internal refinement tolerance. This project already has a documented catastrophe of exactly that form: KP14's G_func.csv was solved under pre-Jun-18 parameters and is wrong by ~49x under current config.py; kp14_fd.py cannot even be re-run because 'from parameters_kp14 import *' refers to a module absent from the repo; and integ_results.npz returns exact zeros over the entire region where 98% of firm-months live, corrupting every downstream KP14 'truth'. Adding three more hand-solved solution files to a codebase with that track record, for a claimed 1.05-1.18x, is not a trade I would sanction. The O(N^2) kron cost also multiplies by M^2 = 9 on terms 3, 5 and 7, in a moments step already pinned to n_jobs = 1 (config.py:40).
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: No. The author's own estimate is 1.05-1.18x, inside the Monte Carlo noise of a single-seed run and unable to survive a standard-error column (the prior 30-replication experiment here found FM 0.2114 sd 0.0149 vs DKKM3600 0.2091 sd 0.0155). Two specific reasons it lands at the bottom of even that range. First, the author flags it: A_xi already correlates -0.975 with 1/mve, so if durability mix correlates with firm size in equilibrium — and it will, since older larger firms hold older longer-lived project stocks — the new dimension collapses back into size and delivers nothing. Second, the classification story ('recover the simplex point from payout yield, agr volatility, and rate-beta') is exactly the sort of target my P1 experiment shows a linear method recovers once handed the right constructed columns; FM given payout*nproj and the rate-beta interaction would close most of it. The author honestly notes the FF size-by-payout double sort may already recover the mix, and proposes engineering the type parameters so no single characteristic orders the types — a milder version of P5's fatal orthogonalisation, attracting the same criticism.
verdicts.salvage: If anything survives, it is the BETA_ZR change ALONE, without durability types: raising corr_zr from -0.175 toward -0.5 makes the interest-rate factor genuinely priced and gives BGN a second priced dimension — the condition the theory actually requires, and which no other proposal except P2 and P5 supplies. That is one config constant plus one Jstar re-solve, not three. Do it as a standalone experiment with a regression test that the old BETA_ZR reproduces the current moments exactly, and report what it does to the affine identity and to the population ceiling. Drop the M-type durability machinery entirely: days of compute, a 9x runtime multiplier, three hand-solved files with no verification, for a gain inside the noise.

missed_ideas: FAIRNESS FIRST — the comparison is currently rigged toward DKKM and no model change can be interpreted until it is fixed. config.py:187 sets ALPHA_LST_FAMA = [0]: FF and FM get plain OLS with zero tuning decisions. Meanwhile bop-analyze-remote/create_slides_tables.py:83-97 (find_best_alpha_for_model) selects DKKM's alpha by argmax/argmin of the reported evaluation metric itself, across all iterations, for each of 4 feature counts — post-hoc oracle selection over 24 cells using the statistic being reported. Before any economics changes, give FF/FM the identical ridge grid and the identical selection rule, or replace the argmax with a single pre-specified alpha for everyone. The current 1.04x BGN gap may not survive that alone. No proposal mentions this, and it is the first thing a referee will strike.

THE ECONOMETRICIAN IS DENIED 1/mve, AND rp IS EXACTLY AFFINE IN IT. From panel_functions_bgn.py:172-186, 1+eret_i = pi*e_t/bond_t + [term1+term3-pi*G_t*e_t/bond_t]*(1/mve_i) + Chat*pi*bm_i. The true premium is an exact linear function of (1/mve, bm). But MODEL_CHARS gives 'size' = log(mve). FM is therefore being asked to span an exactly-linear truth through a nonlinear transform of the right variable, while DKKM's sin/cos basis can approximate the reciprocal. Any DKKM-over-FM gap in the CURRENT baseline may be nothing but that. Add 1/mve (or the earnings-to-price style ratio the model naturally generates) to the characteristic set and re-run the baseline before doing anything else — this single check could reclassify the existing result as an artifact.

NO STANDARD ERRORS ANYWHERE. Every reported gap (BGN DKKM/FF = 1.04x, GS21 = 1.15x) is a single-run point estimate, and several proposals predict effects of 1.05-1.2x. A referee will demand the Monte Carlo distribution across seeds. The prior 30-replication experiment in this project found FM 0.2114 (sd 0.0149) versus DKKM3600 0.2091 (sd 0.0155) — the gap is a small fraction of one standard deviation. Any proposal whose predicted effect is under ~1.3x is not measurable with one seed and should not be attempted without a multi-seed design specified in advance.

THE SPAN PROJECTOR USED THROUGHOUT THE DIAGNOSIS PHASE IS WRONG, AND ALL HEADROOM NUMBERS NEED RECOMPUTING. A linear characteristic method delivers w = X a, so the attainable Sharpe is sqrt(rp' X (X'Sigma X)^{-1} X' rp). The reported figures correspond to w = Sigma^{-1} X a. On the same cross-section (N=1000, band 0.1, X=[1,log mve,bm]) these give 69.4% and 83.4% of max_sr respectively. The BGN diagnosis's '{1,size,bm} attains 91.7%', Proposal 1's '95.03%' and its '69.06%' are all computed against the wrong weight space. Recompute before any decision rests on them.

MEASUREMENT ERROR IN CHARACTERISTICS — cheaper, more general, and more defensible than any of the six. DKKM obtain a 2.6-3.4x complexity gain in real data using the SAME five characteristics. So the count is not the issue; the informational structure is. Here the chars are noiseless, redundant, smoothly invertible functions of 2-3 latent states — exactly the regime where a small correctly-specified model is optimal. Adding classical measurement error, reporting lags, and several redundant-but-imperfect proxies for the same state makes recovering w*(x) genuinely require a rich function class, applies identically to all three models, is one line per characteristic, and is impossible to characterise as tuning. It should have been Proposal 1.

ONE MECHANISM FOR ALL THREE MODELS, NOT THREE TAILORED FIXES. The brief invites per-model alterations and the proposals oblige. But a paper that changes BGN one way, KP14 another and GS21 a third, each until the desired result appears, is three specification searches presented as robustness. The strongest paper picks ONE economically general ingredient (measurement error; a demand wedge; a high-dimensional priced-shock space) and shows it produces the virtue of complexity in all three otherwise-unmodified models. A referee will trust that and will not trust six model-specific dials.

REPORT Sharpe/max_sr, AND PROPAGATE max_sr INTO THE RESULTS FILES. Sharpe_t(w) = max_sr_t * cos_Sigma(w, w*) is an exact identity, so the interpretable quantity is the cosine, not the level. max_sr is already computed in every sdf_loop (sdf_compute_bgn.py:326-328) and saved into *_moments.pkl, but evaluate_sdfs.py never propagates it, so no table shows whether FF at 0.2423 is 30% or 90% of the ceiling. Without it the reader cannot distinguish 'the estimator is failing' from 'the model has nothing to estimate' — the entire question the paper is about. Two-line fix; it should precede everything.

REPORT THE COMPLEXITY CURVE, NOT JUST THE BEST CELL. The diagnostic distinguishing a real virtue-of-complexity result from a shrinkage result is whether Sharpe RISES with P at fixed tuning. It is currently flat (BGN 0.2466 -> 0.2528 from P=6 to P=3600, +2.5%). Several proposals predict a level gap without predicting a rising curve; a level gap with a flat curve is a shrinkage effect and a referee will say so. Every proposal should state its predicted curve shape, and the paper should show it.

MICROCAPS AND THE SIZE DISTRIBUTION. DKKM's real-data Sharpe falls from ~3.7 to ~1.6 in mega/large caps, so much of the empirical virtue of complexity lives in small, high-idiosyncratic-volatility names. BGN's cross-section has sd(log mve) far below CRSP's ~2.0, N is fixed at 1000 with no entry or exit, and there is no fat left tail. A heavier-tailed size distribution with strong size-dependence of both alpha and idiosyncratic variance is a targeted, empirically-anchored change no proposal makes.

TEST ASSETS WITH POWER. generate_25_portfolios.py:107-119 sorts only on mve and bm — two characteristics every method already spans linearly — and compute_pricing_errors.py then runs each method's MVE return as a single factor against them. This test cannot detect nonlinear-in-characteristics mispricing by construction. Add portfolios sorted on interactions (size x bm, roe x agr), on non-monotone transforms, or directly on deciles of the model's TRUE conditional SDF weight. Otherwise the pricing-error evidence is vacuous whichever proposal is adopted.

PRE-REGISTER THE CALIBRATION, AND SHOW THE FAILURES. Several proposals amount to changing one constant (P1's 0.1 -> 1.75) or adding one parameter (P2's SIGMA_KAPPA, P5's THETA_W). The only way these read as science rather than search is if the target moments are stated first, the full scan is shown including settings that do NOT produce the result, and the parameter is pinned by an external moment rather than by the DKKM/FM gap. P1's four-moment scan is closest to this and should be the template; P2 and P5 currently pin their parameters partly by the desired outcome.

CONSIDER PUBLISHING THE NEGATIVE RESULT. The strongest thing in this project is not any of the six proposals — it is the demonstration, with oracle span calculations, that a frictionless representative-agent production model with a rank-1 price-of-risk vector and an exactly-affine cross-section of expected returns CANNOT generate a real-data-sized virtue of complexity, plus the precise identification of which DKKM condition it violates (effective rank of E[FF'] ~ 16 against the several hundred their AIPT calibration requires). A paper that states the necessary conditions, proves the standard models violate them, and then shows the minimal ingredient that restores them is more publishable, and far more robust to a hostile referee, than a paper reporting a tuned 1.4x. Frame the model changes as the CONSTRUCTIVE half of a negative result, not as the result.
